finding: Lane-id ownership mismatch renders the same actor on both sides of ATM_TASK_CLAIM_OWNER_MISMATCH, and bare follow-up commands silently mint a new lane unless the operator keeps ATM_LANE_SESSION_ID bound. This makes valid same-actor recovery look self-contradictory and token-expensive.
expectedBehavior: When ownershipMode is lane-id, the error code and prose should compare lane sessions directly, and lane adopt should persist the adopted session for subsequent commands or emit an explicit env-binding requirement that does not silently remint.
evidenceOrRepro: During ATM-GOV-0243 closeout on 2026-07-29, `tasks renew --task ATM-GOV-0243 --actor codex-git-series-captain --json` returned currentActor and actorId both equal to codex-git-series-captain while holdingLaneSessionId differed from requestedLaneSessionId. Recovery succeeded only after binding ATM_LANE_SESSION_ID to lane-20260729211907-codex-git-series-captain-49242903e2.
followUp: Open a lane-session UX/state-machine task to split lane-vs-actor mismatch codes, persist adopt decisions, and add regression coverage for renew/claim/close after long validators.
